bleeding-control.context: A gauze pad with a cross on top of a forearm and a downward arrow pressing on it. Used for first aid guides, stop-the-bleed training and trauma kits.

cooling-a-burn.context: A hand held flat under a tap with three streams of water running onto it. Used for first aid instructions on treating burns and scalds.

first-aid-sign.context: A rounded square safety sign with a solid white cross in the middle. Used to mark first aid stations, kits and medical rooms.

custodian-helmet.context: A tall domed helmet with a star badge on the front, a knob on top and a flat brim. Used for police, law enforcement and British constable themes.

traffic-wand.context: A glowing baton with a grip at one end and light lines along the shaft. Used for traffic control, airport marshalling and event parking.

police-bicycle.context: A bicycle with a bag over the rear wheel and a small light beam at the front. Used for bike patrol, community policing and cycle officers.

police-blue-lamp.context: A square lantern with glass panels hanging from a bracket on a wall, with light rays to the right. Used for police stations, old-style station signs and law enforcement themes.

missing-person-poster.context: A sheet of paper with a heading bar and a head-and-shoulders portrait. Used for missing person notices, search appeals and have-you-seen-me flyers.

shoulder-radio-mic.context: A small speaker microphone with two grille dots, a side button and a coiled cable hanging from it. Used for two-way radios, officer comms and push-to-talk gear.

traffic-police-podium.context: A round raised stand with a small umbrella canopy held over it on a pole. Used for point duty, traffic control posts and intersection officers.

lost-child.context: A small child figure with arms out standing next to a large question mark. Used for lost child alerts, separated families and find-a-parent points.

safety-officer.context: A person wearing a hard hat and a vest standing beside a clipboard that carries a checkmark. Used for site safety, inspections and compliance checks.

exterior-alarm-box.context: A wall-mounted box with a flashing lamp on top, a speaker grille line and sound marks either side. Used for outdoor sirens, burglar alarms and building alarm sounders.

wedge-barrier.context: A slanted steel plate raised out of the road surface on a support, with a ground line under it. Used for vehicle barriers, checkpoints and security installations.

key-control-cabinet.context: A wall cabinet with its door swung open and four keys hanging from hooks inside. Used for key management, vehicle key storage and facility key control.

bomb-disposal-robot.context: A tracked robot with a camera on its body and a jointed arm ending in a gripper claw. Used for bomb squad, explosive ordnance and remote handling themes.

emergency-exit-sign.context: A rectangular sign with a running figure heading towards an open doorway. Used for escape routes, exits and building safety plans.

break-glass-key-box.context: A wall box with a cracked glass front and a key inside, with a bolt-shaped crack across the corner. Used for emergency key access and break-glass fire alarm keys.

keep-exit-clear-sign.context: A prohibition circle with a slash over a doorway that has a box standing in front of it. Used to tell people not to block fire exits and escape routes.

shelter-in-place.context: A house outline with a person standing inside it. Used for stay-indoors warnings, lockdowns and hazardous release alerts.

stairwell-evacuation.context: Two figures walking down a zigzag staircase one after another. Used for evacuation drills, fire escape stairs and stairs-not-lifts guidance.

emergency-exit-window.context: A rounded vehicle window with a curved arrow showing it swings open and a pull handle along the bottom edge. Used for bus, train and coach emergency exits.

brace-position.context: A side view of a seated person bent forward with head down and arms over the head, behind a seat back. Used for air safety cards and crash preparation guidance.

emergency-cot.context: A low folding bed with crossed legs, a pillow at one end and a folded blanket on the mattress. Used for shelters, relief camps and emergency sleeping areas.

collapsed-building.context: Three floor slabs stacked unevenly and tilted on top of each other, with a piece of debris beside them. Used for earthquake damage and structural collapse.

stranded-on-roof.context: A person with one arm raised on top of a roof ridge that pokes out of wavy water. Used for flood rescue and trapped-by-flood alerts.

flooded-car.context: A car body sunk up to its windows in water with two wavy ripple lines across it. Used for flash flood warnings and do-not-drive-through-water signs.

fallen-tree.context: A round root ball at one end of a tree trunk lying on its side with bare branches, above a road line. Used for storm damage and blocked-road reports.

gas-leak.context: A pipe with a hand-wheel valve on top and a cloud of gas rising from a crack in it. Used for gas escape alerts and evacuation guidance.

burst-pipe.context: A pipe broken into two pieces with water shooting up from the gap in several jets. Used for plumbing emergencies and water main breaks.

oil-spill-boom.context: A ring of round floats around a dark oval oil slick, with a wavy water line below. Used for oil spill response and marine pollution control.

capsized-boat.context: A small hull turned upside down above the water with two wavy lines across it. Used for boating accidents, sinking and water rescue.

person-drowning.context: A head with both arms raised above two wavy water lines. Used for drowning warnings, swimmer-in-distress alerts and water safety.

fallen-through-ice.context: A person up to the chest in a jagged opening in the ice with arms spread on the edge and a little water below. Used for thin-ice warnings and ice rescue.

hot-car-danger.context: A parked car with two heat marks above it and a thermometer standing beside it. Used for heatstroke warnings and never-leave-children-or-pets-in-cars notices.

emergency-broadcast.context: A radio mast sending curved signal waves, with a small warning triangle beside it. Used for public alert systems and emergency radio announcements.

phone-emergency-warning.context: A smartphone showing a large warning triangle with an exclamation mark on its screen. Used for wireless emergency alerts and cell broadcast messages.

orange-smoke-canister.context: A handheld canister with a pull ring at its side and a thick cloud of smoke rising from the top. Used for distress signals and rescue marking.

ration-pack.context: A sealed food pouch with a seal line at the top, a tear notch at the side and a fork printed on the front. Used for emergency food, military rations and relief supplies.

water-purification-tablets.context: Two round scored tablets beside a water drop. Used for water treatment, safe drinking water and emergency supplies.

relief-supplies-box.context: A taped cardboard box with a heart on the front and a water bottle standing beside it. Used for humanitarian aid, donation drives and disaster relief.

food-aid-sack.context: A tied sack with a wheat ear printed on its front. Used for grain deliveries, food relief and famine aid.

supply-airdrop.context: A crate hanging under an open parachute canopy by three lines. Used for aerial aid delivery and cargo drops.

water-distribution-point.context: A standpipe with two taps and a jerry can under one of them, with drops falling from the other. Used for relief camps and clean water access points.

bucket-toilet.context: A bucket with a toilet seat fitted on top and the lid raised behind it. Used for emergency sanitation, camping and disaster toilets.

fallout-shelter-sign.context: A round sign with three downward-pointing triangles arranged inside a ring. Used for civil defense shelters and cold war era refuge markers.

furniture-anti-tip-strap.context: A tall bookcase with two shelf lines beside a wall, fixed to the wall by a short strap at the top. Used for earthquake and child safety home guides.

gas-shutoff-wrench.context: A flat open-ended wrench tilted to one side with a small flame beside it. Used for earthquake kits and turning off the gas supply.

rescue-board.context: A long rescue paddle board with a pointed nose, a cross on the deck and a grab handle near the tail. Used for surf lifesaving and beach rescue.

pool-rescue-hook.context: A long pole with a large curved crook at the top, above a wavy water line. Used for pool safety and reach-assist water rescue.

ice-rescue-picks.context: Two grip handles angled outward with steel spikes pointing down and a cord looped between them. Used for ice safety and self-rescue after falling through ice.

dan-buoy.context: A tall pole with a flag at the top, a rounded float in the middle and a small weight at the bottom. Used for man overboard marking and boating safety.

immersion-suit.context: A one-piece survival suit with a hood showing a small face opening, mitts and boots, and a zip down the front. Used for marine safety and cold water survival.

rescue-strop.context: A padded horseshoe-shaped sling hanging from two straps that meet at a hoist point. Used for helicopter hoists and winch rescues.

no-diving-sign.context: A prohibition circle with a slash over a diver entering the water head first. Used for pool and shoreline signs about shallow water.

arc-flash-hood.context: A heavy protective hood with a wide dark face window and a cape covering the shoulders. Used for electrical safety gear and high voltage work.

reflective-armband.context: A wide band with two stripes wrapped around an upper arm. Used for night visibility gear for runners, cyclists and walkers.

no-smoking-sign.context: A prohibition circle with a slash over a lit cigarette with a curl of smoke. Used for smoke-free areas, hospitals and fuel stations.

no-water-on-fire-sign.context: A prohibition circle with a slash over a tilted bucket pouring drops of water onto a flame. Used for warnings against using water on electrical, oil and grease fires.

no-elevator-in-fire-sign.context: A prohibition circle with a slash over an elevator door beside a flame. Used for fire evacuation signs telling people to use the stairs.

boil-water-notice.context: A cooking pot with bubbles rising from it and a small notice card marked with a water drop. Used for boil water advisories and unsafe tap water alerts.

pacemaker-prohibited-sign.context: A prohibition circle with a slash over a torso carrying a small device on the chest. Used to warn people with pacemakers away from strong magnets and equipment.

no-metal-objects-sign.context: A prohibition circle with a slash over a key and a round watch face. Used for MRI rooms, magnet areas and security screening.

keep-out-sign.context: A rounded square sign with a raised open palm. Used for restricted areas, private property and stop notices.

falling-ice-sign.context: A warning triangle with two icicles hanging from an edge and a small piece of ice falling. Used for winter signs near roofs, bridges and overhangs.

cliff-edge-sign.context: A warning triangle with a stepped cliff edge and a small figure falling over the side. Used for trail and coastal path warnings.

asbestos-warning-sign.context: A warning triangle with a bold letter A inside it. Used for demolition, renovation and building hazard notices.

ladder-hazard-sign.context: A warning triangle with a leaning ladder, its rungs set on a slant, about to tip over. Used for working-at-height and ladder safety notices.

danger-sign.context: A rounded square notice with a solid heading band over two lines of blank text. Used for danger, hazard and site warning boards.

safety-record-board.context: A standing scoreboard with a heading bar and one large digit. Used for days-without-incident counters on worksites.

airport-fire-truck.context: A long fire vehicle in side view with a roof water cannon, a cab on the right and three axles. Used for airport rescue and aircraft firefighting.

brush-fire-truck.context: A pickup-style fire truck with a water tank and hose reel on the flatbed behind the cab. Used for wildland and grass fire response.

heavy-rescue-truck.context: A boxy truck with two roll-up compartment doors along its side and a light bar on the cab roof. Used for technical rescue and extrication units.

mobile-command-vehicle.context: A large bus-shaped vehicle with a row of windows, a satellite dish and an antenna on its roof. Used for incident command posts and field operations.

pedestrian-walkway-sign.context: A round sign with a walking figure standing on a bar that marks a footpath. Used for signs telling people to use the pedestrian route.

team-lift-sign.context: A round sign with two figures lifting a box between them. Used for manual handling rules and heavy-load notices.

incoming-tide-sign.context: A warning triangle with a small figure above two wave lines closing in from below. Used for beach, sandbar and tidal flat warnings.

submerged-rocks-sign.context: A warning triangle with a wavy water line above a row of jagged rocks and a small head at the surface. Used for swimming and boating hazard signs.

max-occupancy-sign.context: A rounded square sign with three small figures above the number ten. Used for room, lift and venue capacity limits.

hydrant-marker-plate.context: A small upright plate with a large letter H and square number marks above and below its crossbar. Used for hydrant locations and fire service signage.
